title: Deep learning assesses stored red blood cell quality from label-free images
summary: A neural network trained on brightfield imaging flow cytometry images agreed with experts on seven red blood cell morphologies in 76.7% of cases, against 82.5% agreement between different experts. A weakly supervised network trained only on storage duration produced a feature space showing chronological morphological change that predicted physiological hemolytic assay readouts better than expert morphology classification. The authors note clinical multi-site testing is needed.
ai_technology: Neural networks on brightfield imaging flow cytometry images (supervised and weakly supervised)
organization: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Ryerson University

evidence.tested: Agreement with expert annotations and comparison of learned features with hemolytic assay readouts of stored blood.
evidence.unknown: Single-site data; multi-site clinical testing not done; full text not reviewed.
